_comment: Single source of truth for the flagos platform/build matrix.
Consumed by setup.py (via json) and by CMake (via string(JSON), see
cmake/FlagosPlatforms.cmake). Editing this file is how a platform's
build switches, runtime source dir, project languages, USE_* macro,
bundled-libtorch dir and wheel local-version tag are changed.
Only genuinely platform-specific SDK path resolution (which env vars,
which default install dir) stays in the CMakeLists files; that is the
SDK-roots phase of issue #376, tracked separately.
_accelerators_comment: kernel_defaults: what the platform builds before any explicit FLAGOS_BUILD_*
environment value. Every platform starts from all-ON; the entries below are
the resolved defaults. setup.py owns this resolution at build time and CMake
applies the same values when a switch was not passed as -D.
pins: values an explicit -D/environment variable may not contradict, because
the platform cannot produce the other answer at all. The reason is shown in
the CMake FATAL_ERROR and mirrors setup.py's ValueError.
pins must equal kernel_defaults for the same switch (a pin states the only
possible value; the default already is it).

ppu._comment: T-Head PPU: CUDA toolchain + a bundled PPU libtorch, no native kernel dir.

_comment: MetaX is a CUDA-boxing build: the generated CUDA boxing kernels
re-dispatch PrivateUse1 -> CUDA into maca's libtorch_cuda.so; the
hand-written mxcc kernels under backends/metax/ are retired. No
MACA-built liboperators exists by default, so the FlagGems C++ wrappers
stay off (an explicit FLAGGEMS_CPP=1 with FLAGGEMS_DIR still wins -- the
MACA case is a documented opt-in). FlagGems Python stays on so the boxing
wheel can route to the python path.
Huawei CANN: ACLNN is the only operator library, FlagGems Python is on by
default (FlagTree Triton), boxing is off (the conf routes nothing to the
CUDA boxing kernels).

FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR.reason: ACLNN is the only operator library the CANN toolkit provides

_comment: TsingMicro Kuiper: no vendor backend directory exists, so FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR
is a no-op, and boxing plus FlagGems Python and C++ stay on by default.
Hygon DTK: the vendor torch is a hipified build registering its HIP
kernels under the CUDA key, so the generated boxing kernels dispatch into
libtorch_hip.so unchanged. No FlagGems liboperators exists for DTK.

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: no FlagGems liboperators.so exists for DTK

_comment: Enflame GCU: no CUDA runtime, topsaten provides the native compute ops
(FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR), ops without a topsaten kernel fall back to CPU.
FlagGems Python shares the same dispatcher; boxing is off.
Moore Threads MUSA: native operator route (mudnn), no CUDA runtime, so
boxing is off and the vendor kernels are mandatory. FlagGems Python is on
for the hybrid path.

FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR.reason: mudnn is the only kernel source this toolchain can build

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: no FlagGems liboperators.so exists for MUSA

_comment: D-Robotics RDK BPU: no per-op kernels, only the runtime layer (UCP
allocator, device/stream stubs) is native. FLAGOS_BUILD_VENDOR stays at the
ON default but compiles nothing (backends/bpu/ does not exist).

FLAGOS_BUILD_FLAGGEMS_CPP.reason: the BPU executes compiled graphs and has no per-operator kernels at all
